# Application loop: from first draft to a submission in Sasha's hand

*Template from Sasha, 2026-11-03 (chat, dictated; recorded close to his words). Applies to every grant, fellowship, accelerator or prize application. First run: MIT Solve 2027 (Global Economic Prosperity Challenge).*

## Meta-description
- **Level / parent:** L2 · Business development (Investor) · parent: [meta-template.md](./meta-template.md); engine: [roasting.md](./roasting.md)
- **Lens(es):** Causal (a fixed sequence of drafts, roasts and abstracts)
- **Shift carried:** PST 93 Vision ↔ Viability Balancing — an application written once and sent → an application that has survived two roasts and two passes through Sasha's own abstract · shift check: Sasha edits the final text by hand and recognizes himself in it
- **What emerges:** a submission-ready application, plus a sharper positioning and project description that carry into the next application
- **As a part of the whole:** the story of the whole told to capital, refined each time it is told

---

## 1. Essence
Hark carries the drafting and the roasting; Sasha works only on the abstract, where his judgment moves the most, and takes the final text into his own hands. One program at a time; each application sharpens the positioning for the next.

## 2. The loop
1. **Draft v1.** Hark writes the full application from the corpus, memory and the program's own questions and limits. Facts that are not in a source are marked GAP, never invented.
2. **Roast v1.** Hark roasts the draft as the program's reviewer would ([roasting.md](./roasting.md): critique rounds, no fixing). Includes the "does this sound machine-written?" pass.
3. **v2.** Hark writes the next version from the roast, in Sasha's voice, within every field limit (counted per field).
4. **Abstract to Sasha.** Hark sends a short abstract of the whole application: the core claims, the story, the numbers, the asks, and the open questions. Not the full text.
5. **Sasha's inputs on the abstract.** He corrects meaning, emphasis, facts and tone at the abstract level.
6. **v3.** Hark turns his inputs into the next full text, then roasts it again.
7. **Abstract again.** Sasha checks what came out at the abstract level.
8. **One more layer if needed** (steps 5 to 7 again). Usually not.
9. **Sasha edits by hand.** He goes into the application himself and edits it directly.
10. **Submit** only on his explicit yes.

## 3. Rules of thumb
- Every claim traceable to a source; one number, one source.
- The abstract is where Sasha's time goes; the full text is Hark's job until step 9.
- Field limits are counted by script per field, never estimated.
- After each submission, carry the sharpened positioning and project description into the next program in the queue, and note what changed.

## 4. Applied in
- MIT Solve 2027, Global Economic Prosperity Challenge: started 2026-11-03 (draft v1, roast and v2 in the Hark project "MIT Solve 2027 Application").
